documents.title: Academic Honesty Guide: Honesty in Academic Work
documents.stance_why: The policy never bans AI; it lists 'Quoting or paraphrasing language from a Large Language Model (LLM) or other AI service without citing this' as a violation and requires acknowledging LLM assistance. AI use is allowed with citation, and instructors set collaboration rules, so permit.
documents.summary: Grinnell's college-wide academic honesty policy, with the integrity review and appeal process. AI appears as one more source: uncited LLM text is a violation and LLM help must be acknowledged. Most of the document is generic integrity and process text.

units.why: The sentence defines what makes a violation: passing off work 'derived from a machine-generated source' as one's own. It is a definition of misconduct binding students, so P36 (misconduct) rather than P19, which concerns what students may have AI produce.

notes: Coder A. Computing and school layers absent in the collect file. Several units on the honesty guide are generic integrity process rather than AI-specific; included because they govern how AI misuse is handled. The translation-software item is a weak AI fit. Uncovered units: instructor no-contact with student after referral, evidentiary thresholds for referral, drop/withdraw hold, record retention, explaining the why to students, co-creating policy with students.
